info.bio:
Jimmy Eat World es una banda estadounidense de rock alternativo formada en 1994 en Mesa, Arizona.

Jimmy Eat World lo formaron en sus inicios Jim Adkins, Zach Lind (amigos desde la guardería) Tom Linton y Mitch Porter. El nombre de la banda no hace referencia a Jim Adkins, sino a uno de los hermanos de Tom Linton. Éste y sus hermanos menores, Jimmy y Ed, estaban siempre peleándose cuando eran pequeños. Jimmy, que era alto y fuerte, siempre solía ganar.

scenes.name: Hardcore en la era del punk-pop: emocore, ska-core y post-hardcore
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Mientras las revistas anuncian la «muerte del punk», el hardcore se convierte en un movimiento que no deja pueblo sin tocar y genera subgéneros. El «emocore» (Jawbreaker, Weezer, Sunny Day Real Estate, Promise Ring, At The Drive-In, Jimmy Eat World, Seaweed); el hardcore progresivo de Washington (Nation Of Ulysses, Make-Up, Shudder To Think, Jawbox, Edsel, Lungfish, Circus Lupus, Dismemberment Plan); el «ska-core» (Operation Ivy, Rancid, Mighty Mighty Bosstones, Sublime, No Doubt); el punk-pop que llega a las listas (Green Day, Offspring, Flop, Pennywise, Pegboy, Superchunk, Queers); el garage-punk californiano (Drive Like Jehu, Rocket From The Crypt, Blink 182, Zen Guerrilla); el jazzcore (Bazooka, Iceburn); la vieja escuela (D Generation, Supersuckers, Zeke, Dropkick Murphys, Silverfish, Turbonegro) y el post-hardcore de Unwound.

podcast.title: Contemporary Powerpop
podcast.body: Jimmy Eat World is identified as one of the contemporary bands that continue the Powerpop tradition. They are listed alongside other groups like OkGo and All American Rejects as modern examples of the genre, showcasing its enduring influence into the present day. "Well we have Jimmy Eat World, OkGo, All American Rejects, Simple Plan, maybe Fallout Boy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Emo Credentials and Mainstream Success
podcast.body: Jimmy Eat World possessed genuine emo credentials and contributed to the widespread popularity of third wave emo through songs that helped the genre achieve significant commercial success. Their rise also coincided with a period where some emo lyrics took a darker turn. "And then there were bands like Jimmy Eat World. They have emo credentials, but they also had songs like, well, this. Thanks to songs like that, third wave emo was huge, but things also got dark."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Contemporary Powerpop Sound
xref.body: Recorded in 1972, their song "Roadrunner" is noted for sounding "every bit as modern powerpop as anything by the strokes or slone, the new pranographers, the Danny Warhol's, Jimmy Eat World, and even the Go-Ghosts, and the knack and blondie and the Romantics," demonstrating its ahead-of-its-time quality. "It was recorded in 1972, and it is every bit as modern powerpop as anything by the strokes or slone, the new pranographers, the Danny Warhol's, Jimmy Eat World, and even the Go-Ghosts, and the knack and blondie and the Romantics."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Leading Emo Band
xref.body: Dashboard Confessional was one of several bands that saw a surge in popularity following Jimmy Eat World's success, as labels actively sought to sign Emo and Emo-ish acts. Their music contributed to the burgeoning Emo scene that gained traction in the early to mid-2000s. "Dashboard, confessional, taking back Sunday, panic at the disco, followed boy, story of the year, funeral for a friend, 30 seconds to Mars."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
